A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe the same SIG/Score2Instruct work. Their complete main texts and supplements, including tables and figures, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of six video LMMs before and after S2I tuning, quality-scoring results, and component and data-scaling ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds benchmark evaluations, comparator results, ablations, alternative-judge evaluations, and a human study.

M1.justification: The automated dimension scoring, discretization, hierarchical CoT, and two-stage tuning procedure remain unchanged. ConvNeXt and QA-generation details are newly disclosed; slow-fast sampling is evaluated as an additional ablation rather than adopted into the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds Q-Bench-Video evaluation covering technical, aesthetic, temporal, and AIGC categories, and uses VQA2 Stage-2&3 instruction data in a training comparison. The original S2I sources, S2I-Bench, and five VQA evaluation sets remain, making this a bounded coverage extension.

E2.justification: New supplementary Tables 2–4 substantially expand comparisons beyond the retained generic LMM baselines: Q-Instruct, Depict-QA, and Qwen2.5-VL-32B for justification; Q-Align, Fast-VQA, and PVQ for scoring; and a VQA2-trained control. These methods now have reported comparative results, rather than merely citations.

E3.justification: Added experiments introduce a VQA2 training-data control, slow-fast sampling, Qwen2.5-32B judging, and a 20-participant human study. Existing one-epoch training, principal metrics, and greedy decoding remain. The newly stated uniform sampling of 16 evaluation frames is disclosure, not an established change to existing experiments.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands diagnostic evidence: automated versus human-annotated instruction data, uniform versus slow-fast sampling, distortion-only versus aesthetic-only dimensions, and agreement across GPT, Qwen, and human judges. Supplementary Tables 4–7 address questions absent from v1 while retaining its original ablations.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging five S2I-Bench evaluations. Neither provides confidence intervals, standard deviations, significance tests, or training-seed information. The added participant count describes the new study's sample size, not a new uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: Main Tables 2–7 and the proprietary-model results remain numerically unchanged, but new supplementary Tables 1–7 add substantial comparative and diagnostic outcomes. For example, the slow-fast variant reports LIVE-VQC SRCC/PLCC of 0.795/0.808 versus uniform sampling's 0.738/0.752. These are different sampling conditions, not a version-to-version gain. Q-Bench-Video's conflicting before/after and SRCC/PLCC labels prevent an unambiguous tuning-gain interpretation.

T1.justification: Neither version introduces formal theorems or proofs. The existing dimension definitions, discretization rationale, and training objectives are retained; the added material is empirical or explanatory.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims about SIG, S2I, S2I-Bench, and simultaneous improvement of scoring and justification. The new title and supplementary novelty discussion shift emphasis without changing these main claims.

C2.justification: The supplement newly acknowledges inferior scoring against specialized comparators and explains the emphasis on scalable instruction generation. It also interprets sampling and dimension ablations, discusses annotation subjectivity and bias mitigation, and uses judge agreement to argue for metric reliability. These qualify and extend the retained interpretations.

D1.justification: v2 discloses uniform 16-frame evaluation, ConvNeXt-based dimension scorers, per-dimension QA curation, and 20 experts performing benchmark checks. It also supplies a repository address where code and data are promised; v1 only promises future release. These improve documentation without establishing changed implementation or actual resource availability.

R1.justification: New supplementary Section 2 explicitly distinguishes the work from FineVQ and VQA2, emphasizing SIG, S2I, and S2I-Bench rather than training-strategy novelty. Citation changes include adding VisualCritic and replacing the VCG attribution to VideoGPT+ with Video-ChatGPT; most other reference changes are bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The title and contact information change, with localized prose and caption rewrites. The supplement gains experimental and novelty sections and reorganizes retained details under new numbering, but most original narrative and prompt text remains substantially intact.

P2.justification: Seven new supplementary tables provide benchmark, comparator, ablation, and judge-agreement displays, and a new figure shows two qualitative cases. Existing main figures and numerical tables are retained, with table relocations and revised captions. Figure 1's caption now names SRCC alone despite retaining the previous plotted values.

improvement.justification: The added specialist comparisons, controlled ablations, and human/alternative-judge checks make the evidence more informative than v1's largely before-and-after LMM comparisons. Acknowledging scoring limitations also improves interpretation. The net gain is limited by sparse protocols for the new comparisons and human study, ambiguous Q-Bench-Video labeling, and the less accurate Figure 1 metric caption.
